KEY MESSAGE 1...
A strong Canadian surface anticyclone over south-central Quebec
continues to funnel dry and chilly air over the forecast area 
this morning. A weak upper level disturbance continues to allow 
for some higher clouds to intermittently stream into the region.
Some patchy to localized areas of frost continue mainly over 
the northern zones, as temps continue to fall into the 30s and 
40s. Some patchy radiational mist in the sheltered valleys and 
near major bodies of water will burn off after daybreak. The 
strong subsidence from the surface high will yield mostly sunny 
skies. Deeper mixing and a sfc pressure gradient between between
the strong high and low pressure near the Mid Atlantic corridor
will yield breezy northeast/east winds 10-15 mph with some 
gusts 20-25 mph with temps running slightly below normal with 
upper 50s to lower 60s over the higher terrain and mid and 
spotty upper 60s in the valleys.

The Rex Block that sets up during the day continues into tonight
with a closed H500 anticyclone over southeast Ontario and the 
Upper Great Lakes Region north of a closed low over the Ohio 
Valley and a mid-level trough over the TN Valley and Mid 
Atlantic Region. The strong sfc high remains over 
south/southeast Quebec yielding near ideal radiational cooling 
conditions again with lows falling into the 30s and lower/mid 
40s. The growing season has ended over the south/southwest 
Adirondacks, where areas to locally widespread frost may occur.
Temps falling into the mid to upper 30s with patchy to locally 
areas of frost over southern VT and portions of the Lake George 
northern Saratoga Region. Some patchy frost is also possible in
the Mohawk/Schoharie Valley and eastern Catskills. The one zone
we may need a Frost Advisory for is southeast Warren County 
later. Most other zones are borderline. The lower to mid 40s are
expected from the Capital District/mid Hudson Valley south and 
east. The NBM was blended with the MAVMOS for lows. Also, some 
localized patchy radiational mist is possible in the major river
and sheltered valleys. The low temps are about 10-15 degrees 
below normal. Temps rebound nicely on Thu trending closer to 
seasonal and it will be breezy, as the coastal low forms well 
off the Mid Atlantic Coast near the Gulf Stream of the western 
Atlantic. Ridging with the Rex Block continues over southeast 
Canada, the Great Lakes Region and Northeast for the day. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... 
Thu night into Fri attention shifts to a developing oceanic or 
coastal low near 35N/70W in the western Atlantic. The evolution 
and development of the storm looks like it will be east of the 
Mid Atlantic Region during this time frame, as multiple short- 
wave disturbances try to phase, but the medium range 
guidance/ensembles and EC/GFS AI still vary on the timing, 
evolution and track of the storm. A shift westward closer to the
coast has occurred with some of the guidance (some of the past
few runs of the GFS and CMC guidance), but the track looks 
slower on some the western most solutions like the latest EC and
some of the ensemble members with impacts not until late Sat 
pm/Sat night. However, the latest GFS is fast moving the wave 
towards Cape Cod and southeast New England Fri night into Sat, 
and then retrograding or meandering the storm back to the 
west/southwest over eastern New England to close the weekend and
open next week. This scenario is more of a eastern most 
solution. The EC would have the intense and deep coastal wave 
move towards Long Island and southeast New England Sat night and
then shift it back to the west/southwest towards coastal NJ on
the past few runs prior to the latest 00Z one before moving it back
northeast late in the weekend. The timing and evolution issues 
make the impacts for eastern NY and western New England 
uncertain, but a shift towards the weekend looks likely if the 
western most scenario or cluster the EC ensemble/AI leans 
toward is correct. However, the NBM and WPC continue to lean 
towards the third scenario or cluster where the storm tracks 
closer to southeast New England/Cape Cod and Long Island for 
periods or occasional bands of showers (light to moderate 
beginning late Fri pm /Fri night) from the I-87 or Hudson Valley
corridor eastward continuing into the weekend before decreasing
Sunday. It will become breezy or brisk as gusty north/northeast
to east winds develop. H850 -u winds anomalies (easterlies) 
become 2 to 4 STDEVs above normal with a strong low-level jet 
late Fri/Sat.

The forecast continues to lean towards the NBM with slight to
low chances (20 to 40%) of showers especially from the Capital 
Region south and east Fri pm-Fri night with chances of rain 
increasing to 40-60% from the Hudson River Valley east across
